I know this article refers to the federal level, but there are also state "death taxes", and they can both cause problems for families. I don't care who you are, or how rich you are, I don't think it's right for the government to try and collect taxes on property, and other monies, that's being transferred to heirs after a death. Especially when taxes have already been paid on that that has already been earned.

My family had to go through this process after my grandparent's died and they weren't that wealthy. My grandfather was mainly a farmer with a hundred or so acres of land so that was the bulk of the estate. After the gov't got their hands on it, the family was left with less than half (I actually think it was more like 40%). So how is it fair that my grandparent's worked hard all their life, paid their taxes, etc. then the family was left with half the estate cause the gov't felt they were owed something? All the land is still in the family, and before each kid could take ownership, they had to pay taxes on it. We were fortunate enough that one of my aunts was able to pay the taxes, and essentially, buy my grandparent's house from her brother's and sisters to keep it in the family.

There was another incident, which for full disclosure I don't have all the details (I tried to get as many as I could), but a man was left his father's land. His father was a farmer, and so was this guy so he didn't have a lot of money. It was several hundred acres in a prime location. Before he could do anything with it, the gov't wanted the taxes paid. He tried to work a deal so he could sell off a few acres to pay the taxes and keep the rest, but they wouldn't allow that.
